paragraphs.text: A [white tea](white:definition) cake from Fujian, the province that is [the home of white tea](fujian-white:definition). The record [names the province only](fujian:on-a-label), so the leaf may come from Fuding, Zhenghe or another county that makes white tea; which one is not recorded.

Pressing white tea is a recent practice. [White tea cakes](fujian-white:cakes) began in the 2000s and spread around 2010, because a cake is smaller and easier to keep and carry than loose leaf. Some are pressed from leaf already aged loose for a few years, so the year 2016 can mark the pressing rather than the picking.

At ten years, this cake is past the seven in the trade's saying that white tea is [tea in its first year, medicine at three and a treasure at seven](fujian-white:ageing). That is a saying, not a tested claim, and no agreed number of years makes a white tea aged.

brewing.text: Gongfu style, use about 1 gram of leaf to 15 to 25 ml of water, for example 5 grams in a 100 to 110 ml gaiwan; weigh it, since the leaf is light and bulky. Silver Needle and young, delicate tea take water below the boil, about 75 to 90°C; older, leafier or aged tea takes water at or near the boil. Start with a steep of 10 to 45 seconds and add a few seconds each round. An aged cake is often rinsed quickly first, and older pressed tea can be simmered on the stove, about 5 grams to 500 ml for 3 to 10 minutes; young, delicate tea is not.

notice.text: Jujube or dried dates, herbs and medicine, wood, honey and dried fruit, a deeper, redder liquor, a thicker, rounder body, and less lift in the scent than a young tea.
